title: RSPSSL: A novel high-fidelity Raman spectral preprocessing scheme to enhance biomedical applications and chemical resolution visualization

citations.claim: Hu et al. proposed RSPSSL, a self-supervised learning scheme for Raman spectral preprocessing that performs both denoising and baseline correction without requiring experimentally obtained ideal reference spectra.

Hu et al. noted that the performance of supervised deep learning approaches for spectral preprocessing is limited by the impossibility of experimentally obtaining ideal noise-free and baseline-free reference spectra, forcing reliance on mathematically simulated training data.

Hu et al. used a GAN-based auxiliary task (RSGAN) to generate high-fidelity and diverse synthetic training spectra from a small set of real Raman spectra, addressing the domain gap between simulated and real data.

Hu et al. designed the RSBPCNN model with a dual-pipeline architecture: a Raman-Patches submodule for local feature extraction via sliding windows, and a Background-Estimation submodule for preliminary baseline fitting, merged through a U-shaped Downsampling-Upsampling block.
Hu et al. demonstrated that their RSPSSL scheme achieved an 88% reduction in RMSE and a 60% reduction in L-infinity norm compared to established preprocessing techniques on experimental Raman data.

Hu et al. identified that classical spectral preprocessing methods such as polynomial fitting, iterative morphological operations, and penalized least squares require manual parameter selection, making them unsuitable for high-throughput and cross-device applications.
Hu et al. demonstrated that their trained RSPSSL model generalizes across different Raman spectroscopy devices, laboratories, excitation wavelengths, and sample types without requiring retraining.

Hu et al. modeled Raman spectra as consisting of three components: Raman peaks (signal), slowly fluctuating background/baseline signals from fluorescence and residual Rayleigh scattering, and noise from cosmic rays, ambient light, and detector dark current.

do_not_claim: This paper does not use algorithm unrolling or deep unfolding
This paper does not address chromatogram baseline correction
This paper does not use penalized least squares methods like BEADS as part of its network architecture
This paper does not claim to handle all types of spectroscopy, only Raman spectroscopy
